detail_json.project_description: Chanzi are a protein rich, animal feed producing company, located in Tanzania, and with expansions in place for Kenya as well. Their high protein animal feed is produced through the farming of Black Soldier Flies, and the use of their larvae either in whole form, or dried crushed form. The Black Solider Fly (BSF) is a particular species of fly that is commercially farmed around the world, for its ability to be converted into an insect-based animal feed. Its name comes from the color of the adult flies, which are black with metallic reflections. The commercialization of farming BSF’s came from the large demand for animal feed around the world and the concerns that fish meal and/soy-based meal (animal feed) would in the long term not be a sustainable solution. The larvae are fed organic food waste, which come from a variety of sources, i.e. pre-consumer and post-consumer at industrial and household levels. This organic waste would have otherwise been sent to landfill, thus ensuring recovery for beneficiation of this waste. This diverting of organic waste from a landfill leads to the avoidance of carbon emissions and can therefore potentially be registered as a process which generates carbon credits.
